declared_purpose: Generate financial analysis reports with SVG trends from uploaded financial files and Feishu/local/pasted data. HTML generation is explicitly required; PDF, DOCX and Markdown are additional formats. The workflow prescribes Feishu file delivery and makes web benchmarking optional. The executable implements Excel processing and local conversion; API calls are documented workflow examples (SKILL.md:3–10,18–27,31–84; README.md:9–14,67–71).

data_operations.data_scope: channels.feishu.appId and channels.feishu.appSecret; reading or disclosing the entire configuration is not instructed.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calling agent or shell performing Feishu authentication.

data_operations.operation: Authenticate remotely and receive a token
data_operations.data_scope: app_id and app_secret sent in JSON; returned tenant_access_token assigned to TOKEN.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal; token retained in a shell variable.
data_operations.condition: Executing the documented token request for Feishu access.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve a message to obtain an attachment identifier
data_operations.data_scope: message_id and bearer token sent; unfiltered message API response returned, with fields unspecified in the package.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: open.feishu.cn/open-apis/im/v1/messages/{message_id}; response goes to the calling shell's standard output.
data_operations.condition: Attachment acquisition requires obtaining file_key from the message.

data_operations.data_scope: message_id, file_key and bearer token sent; complete selected attachment downloaded.
data_operations.condition: Following the documented chat attachment path.

data_operations.operation: Acquire financial data through document tools
data_operations.data_scope: Linked document or table financial data; exact arguments and returned fields are unspecified.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: feishu_doc or feishu_bitable tools; backend recipients and storage are unresolved.
data_operations.condition: Second acquisition option in the documented try order.

data_operations.operation: Create a workbook from pasted text
data_operations.data_scope: Parsed pasted content saved as XLSX.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: A workbook file; location and conversion implementation are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Pasted-text acquisition option; an existing local file is instead used directly.

data_operations.data_scope: pip installation requests and resulting packages; financial files are not supplied as installation arguments.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local pip process and Python package environment; any configured remote package source is unspecified.
data_operations.condition: openpyxl import fails, or Markdown conversion reaches its fallback after pandoc fails. The Markdown fallback invokes pip before importing markdownify.

data_operations.operation: Read a workbook and retain first-sheet values
data_operations.data_scope: Workbook loaded with data_only=True; all iterated first-sheet cell values collected into label-keyed rows and header data.
data_operations.condition: Report generation through the supplied executable, including an existing local file used directly.

data_operations.operation: Select periods, identify forecasts and produce trends
data_operations.source: Parsed worksheet labels, headers and values
data_operations.data_scope: Annual and forecast columns, matched financial metrics, aggregate employee count, free cash flow and SVG trends. Forecast status is taken from source metadata.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local report-generation memory and generated report content.
data_operations.condition: Recognized period metadata selects annual/forecast columns; absent recognized metadata, all columns are selected.

data_operations.operation: Derive financial measures and company characterizations
data_operations.source: Selected financial values and source forecast values
data_operations.data_scope: Growth, CAGR, financial ratios, revenue per employee, profitability/liquidity judgments and forecast-based profit-turnaround statements. Industry and risk sections also contain fixed pharmaceutical narratives.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local report content, subsequently included in saved or delivered reports.
data_operations.condition: Numeric analyses depend on available values and sufficient actual periods; several industry risks and opportunities are unconditional once an actual period exists.

data_operations.source: Selected metrics, derived analysis, company and ticker arguments
data_operations.data_scope: Report tables, trends, narratives and company identification. Filename derives from company or input basename.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local {output_dir}/{base_name}_report.html; output_dir defaults to the current directory.
data_operations.condition: Every successful generation path; retaining an HTML output is an explicit format requirement.

data_operations.operation: Convert and persist an additional report format
data_operations.data_scope: Complete report passed by local path to wkhtmltopdf, a Chromium-family browser or pandoc; markdownify fallback reads HTML into memory.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local converter process or library and PDF/DOCX/Markdown output file. wkhtmltopdf receives --enable-local-file-access; browser invocations receive --no-sandbox.
data_operations.condition: A non-HTML format is selected; PDF is the default. Additional output depends on conversion succeeding.

data_operations.operation: Return generation status to the caller
data_operations.source: Output paths, HTML length and conversion outcome
data_operations.data_scope: Report filenames and directories, HTML byte count, output format and success/failure status.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Standard output of the calling process; no further logging destination is specified.
data_operations.condition: HTML is written or an additional conversion is attempted.

data_operations.data_scope: Query containing company, year and industry-comparison/market-share terms.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: web_search tool; search backend and retention are unspecified. Results may return to its caller.
data_operations.condition: Optional workflow enhancement; no web-search invocation is implemented in the generator.

data_operations.data_scope: Complete report.html content, file_name, file_type and bearer token; returned upload response and file_key are assigned to shell variables.
data_operations.condition: Executing the documented delivery workflow. The example uploads HTML, not the source workbook.

data_operations.operation: Share the uploaded report with a chat
data_operations.data_scope: Chat identifier, file reference, message type and bearer token.
data_operations.condition: Delivery after uploading the report; actual chat membership is unspecified.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated first-sheet rows and unused period values retained alongside report data.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local Python rows dictionary and associated parsing memory.
potential_excess.condition: Input contains values beyond those required for selected metrics and period/forecast detection.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Financial report generation requires selected metrics and metadata; retaining every worksheet value is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Inspect enough source data to preserve metric matching, headers, period selection and forecast detection.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Stream or stage metadata detection and metric selection, discarding unrelated values and unused periods once their relevance is resolved.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve duplicate-label handling, keyword match order, metadata discovery and the all-columns fallback. This narrows retained data within the required read.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete downloaded source workbook after report generation.
potential_excess.condition: Following the documented attachment workflow without external cleanup; supplied generation code does not delete this staging file.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The download supports analysis and report delivery. Continued retention of a skill-created input copy is not required by the declared outcome.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep the input available through parsing and any required retry.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Delete the skill-created staging workbook after successful processing or a bounded retry period.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not delete user-owned originals or requested reports. Preserve the explicitly required HTML output.

potential_excess.data_scope: Redundant pip installation/check for an already available markdownify package; package identifier and installation metadata.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local pip process and package environment; configured package source if contacted.
potential_excess.condition: Markdown conversion falls back from pandoc while markdownify is already importable.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Markdown conversion requires the converter library, but does not require invoking package installation on every fallback.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Import markdownify and convert the required HTML.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Attempt the import first; invoke dependency installation only when the import fails, or use a preinstalled dependency.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the pandoc-first behavior and working Markdown fallback. This removes a redundant action; actual network traffic depends on pip configuration and state.

unknowns: Partial coverage concerns the advertised PDF/CSV input paths, pasted-text conversion and Feishu Doc/Bitable implementations: their extraction logic and detailed data boundaries are absent. The supplied executable reads workbooks through openpyxl (SKILL.md:3–5,49–51; scripts/generate_report.py:23–34).
Feishu response schemas, service retention, uploaded-file expiration, access controls and actual target chat membership are unspecified. The supplied workflow contains no remote deletion request.
The web_search backend, logging, retention and incorporation of returned benchmarks into the report are unspecified. Script-generated industry narratives do not establish external benchmarking.
Third-party libraries, pip package sources and converter internals are outside the supplied source. Additional network requests, filesystem reads, caches or telemetry cannot be established.

Company/ticker, header-derived dates and nonnumeric metric strings are interpolated into HTML without shown escaping. Whether particular inputs cause additional resource reads or disclosure during viewing/conversion is unresolved, including under wkhtmltopdf's local-file-access flag (scripts/generate_report.py:66–82,408–412,450–478,500–505,662–676).
Credential clearing and host-managed cleanup are unspecified. No skill-defined retention period or deletion procedure is provided for local reports or remotely uploaded reports.
